title: Cursor as a Planner
shortDescription: Think of Cursor as a strategic planning partner that helps break down complex tasks into manageable steps.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can analyze your goals and create a step-by-step implementation plan
It helps identify dependencies and suggests the order of operations
You can ask Cursor to outline the architecture before writing code
It can break large features into smaller, testable components
Cursor helps you think through edge cases and potential issues upfront

title: Cursor as a Pair Programmer
shortDescription: Cursor acts like a collaborative coding partner, working alongside you in real-time to solve problems together.
detailedExplanation: Cursor understands context from your open files and recent changes
It can suggest code improvements as you type
You can have back-and-forth conversations about implementation approaches
Cursor helps debug issues by understanding error messages and stack traces
It learns from your codebase style and preferences over time

title: Cursor as a Code Reviewer
shortDescription: Use Cursor to review code for bugs, style issues, and potential improvements before committing.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can analyze your code for common bugs and anti-patterns
It suggests improvements for readability and maintainability
You can ask Cursor to review specific functions or entire files
It helps identify security vulnerabilities and performance issues
Cursor can explain why certain code patterns might be problematic

title: Cursor as a CI Fixer
shortDescription: When CI fails, Cursor can help diagnose and fix test failures, lint errors, and build issues.
detailedExplanation: Cursor reads error messages and stack traces to understand what went wrong
It can fix failing tests by understanding test expectations
Cursor helps resolve linting errors and code style violations
It suggests fixes for type errors and compilation issues
You can paste CI logs and ask Cursor to identify the root cause

title: Cursor as a Knowledge Retriever
shortDescription: Cursor can search through your codebase, documentation, and external resources to answer questions.
detailedExplanation: Cursor indexes your entire codebase for fast retrieval
It can find where functions are defined and how they're used
Cursor searches through documentation files and comments
It can reference external documentation and libraries
You can ask 'where is X used?' or 'how does Y work?' and get precise answers

title: Cursor as a Teacher
shortDescription: Think of Cursor as an educational mentor that explains code concepts, teaches best practices, and helps you learn as you code.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can explain how code works in plain language, breaking down complex algorithms and patterns
It teaches best practices by suggesting improvements and explaining why certain approaches are better
You can ask Cursor to explain unfamiliar code or concepts you encounter in your codebase
Cursor provides context-aware explanations that reference your specific code and project structure
It helps you learn new technologies by generating examples and walking through implementation details
